source_pdf: 312 Affidavits by Indians who accepted land patents under protest 1928 [1 of 3].pdf

extraction.Name: Berry Martin
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want his patent in fee at the time he accepted it, but was told that it was necessary for him to take it, and he did so
extraction.Buyer: sold to J. W. Good, of Chadron, Nebraska, for $800.00, half in cash and half in a horse deal
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: he had to sell it, being behind in taxes
extraction.Occupation/Income: the only income he has is by farming his wife's allotment, and sometimes he works for a neighbor, day labor
extraction.NOTES: mentally incompetent, health not good, as he complains with headaches and rheumatism; has a wife and four children to support; wife's health is poor, childrens' health good; he considers $800.00 a very poor price for his land; has never received any help from the County or the Government; document sworn November 20, 1928
